record.what_it_does: Pylon is a B2B customer support/helpdesk platform (ticketing, AI agents, knowledge base, account intelligence) that companies use to support their business customers.
record.auth_notes: The REST API uses a static Bearer token that only Admin users can generate in Pylon settings (Authorization: Bearer <token>). Separately, Pylon's own hosted MCP server uses OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit) so an AI tool can act as a logged-in dashboard user, but this OAuth flow is specific to the MCP server, not a general third-party OAuth grant for the REST API.
record.access_notes: Pylon has no self-serve signup or free trial; the pricing page only offers 'Book a Demo', and account access is granted after an order form/contract. Once a customer, only Admin users can create API tokens (admin-issued, not per-developer self-serve).
record.main_blocker: No self-serve signup — becoming a Pylon customer requires a sales demo/contract before any API credentials (admin-issued tokens or MCP OAuth) can exist.

evidence.quote: The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you'll need to pass your API token in the header
Auth: OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit). Actions are performed on behalf of the authenticated user
Only Admin users can create API tokens.
The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol
Webhooks are user-defined HTTP callbacks that are triggered by specific events within Pylon.

record.open_questions: Exact rate limits and whether the OpenAPI spec is offered for direct import (vs. only backing the docs site) were not fully verified; also unclear if any lower-cost/non-enterprise Pylon plan exists that includes API access without a sales conversation.
